codeQuality.summary: Critical SQL injection vulnerabilities in three functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) that directly interpolate user input into SQL queries. These are severe security issues that could allow attackers to extract, modify, or delete database contents. Additionally, the code lacks comprehensive error handling, input validation, audit logging, and uses a weak ID generation algorithm.

testCoverage.summary: Critical test coverage gaps in three new search functions. Estimated 35% overall coverage. Most critical gaps: getTodosByUser (authorization vulnerability), searchTodos (SQL injection), and searchTodosByStatus (type confusion and validation). Input sanitization and error handling paths largely untested. Immediate testing required before PR approval.

refactorings.summary: Critical refactoring needed to fix SQL injection vulnerabilities through standardized parameterized queries. Repository/Query Builder pattern would eliminate duplication. Strategy pattern for search operations would improve maintainability. High-impact improvements possible through security-focused refactoring.

recommendations.description: Three critical SQL injection vulnerabilities in new search functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser). Replace template literals and string concatenation with parameterized queries immediately. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to execute arbitrary SQL code.
getTodosByUser function lacks authorization checks. Must add tests verifying users can only access their own todos. This is a data privacy vulnerability that could expose todos from other users.
Three new search functions lack comprehensive input validation tests. Need tests for null/undefined inputs, SQL injection attempts, type confusion (searchTodosByStatus), and edge cases.
Database operations throughout the file lack try-catch blocks and error logging. Add comprehensive error handling to prevent sensitive error details from reaching clients and enable debugging.

Inconsistent SQL query construction between existing CRUD functions (parameterized) and new search functions (string interpolation). Refactor using Query Builder or Repository pattern to standardize all database operations.
ID parameters in multiple functions lack validation before database queries. Add format validation to getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, and deleteTodo functions.
generateId function uses weak algorithm (Date.now() + Math.random()). Replace with cryptographically secure UUID v4 to prevent ID prediction and collision attacks.
No logging for critical operations (create, update, delete). Add audit logging to track who performed what actions and when, required for compliance and security investigations.
Database results are cast directly to Todo type without runtime validation. Add type guards or validation functions to ensure database schema matches expected types.
getAllTodos fetches all records without pagination, could impact performance on large datasets. Add limit/offset parameters and consider eager loading for related data.
